records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling in the parking lot and pulling a 16ft trailer for a parade. the trailer was occupied with multiple individuals participating in the parade. as unit 1 moved through the parking lot at a slow speed. the pedestrian attempted to jump onto the trailer, even after being warned by participants on the trailer not to attempt to get onto the trailer. the pedestrian failed to heed warnings given by participants on the trailer and attempted to jump onto the trailer. the pedestrians leg made it over the rail of the trailer, but she was unable to make it fully into the trailer. the pedestrian fell down and her left arm got caught between the dual axel wheels, while one leg was still inside the trailer. the pedestrian was dragged with her arm between the wheels for approximately 34 feet, with her leg still inside the trailer. passengers on the trailer yelled for the driver to stop, but the driver was unable to hear the yells initially due to parade noise and distance from the trailer. once the driver heard the request, she immediately stopped the vehicle. and other subjects not on the trailer assisted with moving the pedestrian's leg off the trailer and free her arm from the wheels. in the investigator's opinion, the pedestrian should have heeded warnings not to attempt to get onto the trailer. the pedestrian attempted to jump onto the trailer and fell when doing so causing her leg to get stuck on the trailer rail and her arm to fall between the dual axle wheels.

the parking lot; the headlights and overhead white lights on my patrol vehicle lighted the area. ----an overview of the standardized field sobriety test----the standardized field sobriety test (sfst) is a battery of three tests administered and evaluated in a standardized manner to obtain validated indicators of impairment and establish probable cause for arrest. these tests were developed as a result of [roadway] traffic safety administration (nhtsa) and conducted by the southern california research institute. the three tests of the sfst are horizontal gaze nystagmus (hgn), walk and turn (wat), and one leg stand (ols). these tests are administered systematically and are evaluated according to the measured responses of the suspect. ----horizontal gaze nystagmus test----nystagmus is an involuntary jerking or bouncing of the eyes that occurs when there is a disturbance of the vestibular (inner ear) system or the oculomotor control of the eye. hgn refers to lateral or horizontal jerking when the eye gazes to the side. in the impaired driving context, alcohol consumption or consumption of certain other central nervous system depressants, inhalants, or phencyclidine, hinders the ability of the brain to correctly control eye muscles, therefore causing the jerk or bounce associated with hgn. as the degree of impairment becomes greater, the jerking or bouncing, i. e. the nystagmus, becomes more pronounced. this is assessed in the hgn test. before beginning the hgn test, i evaluated olivia for the following to ensure they would be a qualified candidate for evaluation: equal pupil size, resting nystagmus, and equal tracking. i instructed olivia to follow the top of my pen with her eyes only and not to move her head. olivia stated she understood the instructions. olivia did not show any clues indicating intoxication:the following are the clues:-lack of smooth pursuit. -distinct and sustained nystagmus at maximum deviation.-onset of nystagmus prior to 45 degrees. -vertical nystagmus.----walk and turn----the walk and turn test, and one leg stand test are ""divided attention"" tests that are easily performed by most unimpaired people. they require the participant to listen to and follow instructions while performing simple physical movements. impaired persons have difficulty with tasks requiring their attention to be divided between simple mental and physical exercises. i explained and demonstrated the test to olivia, who stated she understood the instructions. olivia consented to perform the test. olivia showed the following clues indicating intoxication:-can't balance during instructions.-misses heel to toe.-uses arms for balance. olivia did not show the following clue indicating intoxication:-steps off the line.-wrong number of steps.-began test before being instructed to.-stops while walking.-turned improperly.----one leg stand----i explained and demonstrated the test to olivia, who stated he understood the instructions. olivia consented to perform the test. the test consists of the following clues indicating intoxication:olivia showed the following clues indicating intoxication:-uses arms for balance.-puts foot down. olivia did not show the following clue indicating intoxication:-sways.-hops. due to olivia's performance during the sfst and my observations made during the initial contact, i determined olivia was not intoxicated while operating a [roadway]. olivia was crying and upset about the collision. she asked several times about the status of deangelia. other family members arrived and drove her home and drove her vehicle home for her. i later spoke with the medic who responded to the scene (medic 37). he stated that deangelia's status had changed. he reported deangelia had a collapsed lung and was bleeding internally from an unknown source. he estimated her condition as life-threatening but stable. deangelia was being moved into surgery while we spoke on the phone. i spoke with deangalia on the phone on [date]. [medical facility] for a long time and reported she had broken bones.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling [roadway]. unit 2, a juvenile, was riding a battery-powered ride-on child's toy on the roadway. unit 1 stated that he failed to observe unit 2 due to being distracted by a mechanical issue inside of the vehicle. unit 1 stated he heard a strange noise and slowed to a stop. unit 1 then observed unit 2 underneath his vehicle. i observed unit 2, a juvenile, lying underneath unit 1 on the passenger side near the front tire. near unit 2 was the ride-on child’s toy vehicle that was badly damaged. during the course of my investigation, i observed the distance from the front tire of the vehicle to the area of impact to be 279. 1 feet. the markings on the roadway did not appear to be made from braking but instead appeared to be from the battery-powered ride-on vehicle sliding across the roadway. fairmiles advised that he had not seen anyone on the roadway but advised the curve in the roadway obscured his view. as i walked the scene, i noticed that the curve was wide and that visibility was high. based on the evidence found in the roadway, and the lack of evidence found in the grass, it is believed that unit 2 was in the roadway at the time of the crash. this investigation is still ongoing.

records.deidentified_narrative: see related sn# [phone]. this is the 110th traffic fatality for the dallas police department for 2023. unit 1 was traveling n/b [roadway], west of the east curb. unit 2 (pedestrian) was walking w/b across the n/b traffic lanes of [roadway]. witness was traveling s/b [roadway], east of the west curb. unit 2 failed to yield right of way-motor vehicle, entered into the path of unit 1 and was struck by the front right of unit 1 and was thrown to the grown. after striking unit 2, driver of unit 1 drove off without stopping to check on unit 2 or stopped to call 9-1-1 as required by state law. unit 2 was crossing the roadway where there was no crosswalks present. when dallas fire department arrived on scene, they found no vital signs on unit 2 at 6:33a. m. witness left his information to patrol officers when they arrived. witness stated as he was traveling s/[roadway]. that he observed unit 1 strike unit 2 [roadway] off. witnesses' vehicle was equipped with an in-car video that captured the incident. i/o has witnesses' information. the crash scene and all interviews were recorded on body worn camera. the video and or photos were saved to evidence. com on id #23-1999046. a 3d laser scan of the scene was done, and detectives with the vehicle crimes unit came out. this report will be incomplete pending the blood toxicology results for unit 2. ** on [date], this supplement was made to add the blood toxicology results for unit 2. unit 2's blood did not have the presence of ethanol but did have the presence of drugs (amphetamine: 13. 3 ng/ml, methamphetamine: 238. 2 ng/ml and carboxytetrahydrocannabinol: 2. 6 ng/ml). this report is now complete.
